# Koolitutka frontend

The frontend is a static Vite and TypeScript application. It runs fully in the
browser and reads a generated SQLite database with `sql.js`, so deployment does
not need a PHP or database backend.

## Source and generated files

Frontend source code lives in `frontend/src/`.

Static source assets live in `frontend/static/`. The header image
`frontend/static/tuulikotka.png` is a source asset and should be committed.

The browser database `frontend/static/koolitutka.sqlite` is generated from the
local `db.sqlite` file by `scripts/export_public_db.py`. It is intentionally not
committed.

The production build is written to `public/`. That directory is generated by
Vite and is intentionally not committed. Serve `public/` as the static web root
for deployment.

## Requirements

- Node.js and npm
- Python 3
- A generated `db.sqlite` from `update_database`

Install frontend dependencies once:

```sh
npm install
```

## Development

Export the browser database when `db.sqlite` has changed:

```sh
npm run export-db
```

Start the local development server:

```sh
npm run dev
```

The development server serves files from `frontend/` and copies files from
`frontend/static/`.

## Production build

Build the deployable static site:

```sh
npm run build
```

This runs the database export first and then writes the final files to
`public/`.

For production deployments, set the canonical site URL so social link previews
can use absolute Open Graph image and page URLs:

```sh
VITE_SITE_URL=https://koolit.hamit.fi/ npm run build
```

The built frontend uses relative paths, so `public/` can be served from a domain
root or from a subdirectory such as `/koolitutka/`. Copy the whole contents of
`public/` together and keep the generated file layout intact so `index.html`,
`koolitutka.sqlite`, `tuulikotka.png`, and `assets/` stay in the same directory
tree. No runtime path configuration is needed for normal static hosting.

## Tests

Run the frontend tests with:

```sh
npm run test
```
